concept: The story is an absence that becomes an opening. The hero puts the missing stars in grey (Sindhu, Lakshya and Satwik-Chirag are skipping it) and the opportunity in white (India's next wave has the seeds), with 5 of 8 and No.1 as the proof underneath. Slide 2 blows up the single number that tells the story, 5 of 8 Indian seeds in women's singles. Slide 3 shows why they earned those seeds (this season's titles), slide 4 is the one record on the line (Treesa-Gayatri's hat-trick bid) and the last slide lists the other title hopes before handing fans the pick. Indian orange, type and shapes only: no player photos, no BWF or event logos.
caption:
Sindhu, Lakshya and Satwik-Chirag are skipping it. India's next wave has the seeds.

The Syed Modi International, a $250,000 Super 300, starts today in Lucknow. Five of the eight women's singles seeds are Indian, led by second seed Tanvi Sharma. Three of them have won World Tour titles this season: Tanvi in Taipei, Ashmita Chaliha in Korea and Devika Sihag in Thailand.

Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand won in 2024 and 2025. They start as top seeds, chasing three in a row. HS Prannoy is third seed in men's singles.

Which Indian wins a title in Lucknow? Tell us below.

Via myKhel, UNI, The Tribune and RevSportz.
